title: Map and list split view
description: A location-browsing layout with a result list and an interactive map side by side, kept in sync: hovering or focusing a list item highlights its marker, selecting a marker scrolls to and highlights the item, and moving the map can update the list ("search this area").
intent: Let users compare places both by details and by location without switching views.
characteristics: list and map share one selection state
markers numbered or labeled to match list items
explicit "search this area" instead of auto-refresh on every pan
list is the accessible primary view; the map is a supplement
interaction: Selection syncs both ways; map pan/zoom never steals page scroll on touch (two-finger or explicit activate); filters apply to both views.
responsive: On narrow screens, a List/Map segmented toggle replaces the split; selected item shows as a bottom card over the map.
accessibility: Everything available on the map is also in the list (address, distance); map has a label and is skippable; markers that are focusable have names matching list items; do not trap keyboard focus in the map.
limitations: Requires a map provider whose license and API terms you must check separately.
Thousands of markers need clustering and server-side bounds queries.
